cell_cycle_time_pz.conditions: human distal femur, ages 5-8 y; the derivation is stated in full - new cells per day = growth rate / mean hypertrophic cell height = 38 um/day / 33 um = 1.2 per day, and cycle time = 24 proliferating cells / 1.2 = 20 days
cell_cycle_time_pz.uncertainty: derived quantity, and derived from the growth rate it would be used to predict. Two further assumptions are load-bearing and both are stated by the authors: (i) the cell height IS the whole axial advance per cycle, i.e. matrix synthesis contributes nothing to elongation, which rat stereology contradicts (wilsman1996: cells are 50-69% of the volume removed at the junction); (ii) the proliferating fraction of the columnar zone is two-thirds, a ratio taken from the RABBIT, applied to a measured human count of 36 maturing-plus-proliferating cells to give 24.

A 20% rise in growth rate is accounted for almost entirely by a 23% rise in terminal cell HEIGHT (31.2 -> 38.5 um, P<0.02) with a 14% FALL in lateral diameter (29.9 -> 25.6 um, P<0.03). terminal_cell_shape_modulation.parameter: matrix volume produced per cell
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.conditions: rat proximal tibia, unchanged during BOTH acceleration (21-35 d) and deceleration (35-80 d)
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.uncertainty: not significantly different in either comparison. Matrix is a large contributor to elongation but is not a regulator of it - the authors' own conclusion is that cartilage matrix plays a subordinate role in regulating growth rate.

terminal_cell_shape_modulation.parameter: contribution of cell height vs proliferative cell number to MECHANICALLY altered growth rate
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.conditions: rat and cattle vertebral and proximal tibial plates plus rabbit proximal tibia, sustained compression or distraction altering growth rate by up to 53%; final (maximum) chondrocytic height in the hypertrophic zone against number of proliferative chondrocytes per unit width
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.uncertainty: overall correlation coefficients 0.38 (proliferative number) and 0.56 (chondrocytic height). REPLICATES hunziker1989's ranking - cell enlargement contributes more than proliferation - in a DIFFERENT laboratory, a DIFFERENT perturbation (mechanical rather than developmental) and three species. It does not replicate the height/volume dissociation, because only height was measured.

terminal_cell_shape_modulation.parameter: correlation of mean hypertrophic cell height with mechanically modulated growth rate
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.conditions: rat caudal vertebrae, 60% bodyweight compression (n=3) or distraction (n=4) for four weeks; growth 53% and 110% of control respectively. Hypertrophic zone height r=0.69, regression slope of cell height on position r=0.37
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.uncertainty: CUTS AGAINST a pure shape account: the authors state the percentage changes in chondrocyte dimensions were SMALLER than the percentage changes in growth velocity, so under mechanical loading cell height does NOT fully account for the growth change - unlike hunziker1989's physiological comparison, where +23% height carried +20% growth almost exactly. Effects were also larger for compression than distraction, i.e. asymmetric.

terminal_cell_shape_modulation.parameter: hypertrophic phase duration under pharmacological rescue
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.conditions: hypophysectomised rat, untreated then infused with IGF-I then with GH
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.uncertainty: DIRECTLY QUALIFIES the invariance recorded from hunziker1989. Hypertrophic phase duration is constant at 45-51 h across PHYSIOLOGICAL states in normal rats, but GH more than halves it in a hypophysectomised one. Pharmacology moves a parameter physiology holds fixed. Whether the same is possible above a normal baseline, rather than in rescue from deficiency, is untested.

terminal_cell_shape_modulation.parameter: proliferating and stem cell cycle time under pharmacological rescue
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.conditions: hypophysectomised rat, untreated then IGF-I then GH
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.uncertainty: GH shortens the proliferating cell cycle nearly four-fold and the stem cycle six-fold. hunziker1989 found cycle time changes cancelled against growth fraction during PHYSIOLOGICAL acceleration; under hormone rescue they do not cancel. The two regimes use different levers.

terminal_cell_shape_modulation.parameter: terminal cell height and volume under pharmacological rescue
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.conditions: hypophysectomised rat; both mean cell volume and cell height were significantly reduced by hypophysectomy at proliferative and hypertrophic stages and restored by either IGF-I or GH
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.uncertainty: restored, not exceeded - the experiment cannot say whether either agent pushes height ABOVE normal. Cell productivity (increase in volume, height and matrix per unit time) did NOT reach normal with either agent and was inversely proportional to cycle time. Matrix volume per cell was similar in normal, treated and untreated groups, consistent with hunziker1989.

terminal_cell_shape_modulation.parameter: chondrocyte shape index, proliferative zone
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.conditions: mouse tibia at E15.5, atomic force microscopy overview images; cells 5-7 um long axis, moderately flattened, oriented along the mediolateral axis before columns have formed
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.uncertainty: embryonic and proliferative-zone, so not the terminal hypertrophic cell this node is about; recorded because it is the only directly measured chondrocyte shape index in growth plate cartilage

terminal_cell_shape_modulation.parameter: elastic modulus of pericellular vs interterritorial matrix
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.conditions: mouse growth plate mid-proliferative zone, AFM; territorial matrix-PCM 1.6 +/- 0.01 kPa, interterritorial matrix 3.6 +/- 0.1 kPa, tracking collagen fibril density
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.uncertainty: the cell sits in a SOFTER shell inside a STIFFER matrix, a 2.25-fold ratio. This is the mechanical architecture an anisotropic-constraint account of shape modulation requires, measured for the first time - but it is a radial measurement in the proliferative zone, and nobody has measured whether the constraint differs axially versus laterally, which is what would actually channel expansion into height.

terminal_cell_shape_modulation.parameter: out-of-plane (axial) Young's modulus, growth plate
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.conditions: newborn bovine distal ulnar growth plate, 4 mm disks, unconfined and confined compression stress-relaxation to 10% strain, transversely isotropic biphasic fit; E3, measured IN COMPRESSION along the growth axis. n=20 paired
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.uncertainty: +/- 0.11 SD. Chondroepiphysis is 1.07 +/- 0.27, so growth plate is half as stiff and twice as permeable. Poisson ratio nu31 = 0 for both tissues; nu21 = 0.30 +/- 0.20.

terminal_cell_shape_modulation.parameter: transverse Young's modulus, growth plate
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.conditions: same specimens; E1, measured IN TENSION in the transverse plane
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.uncertainty: +/- 1.21 SD; chondroepiphysis 10.63 +/- 2.72.

terminal_cell_shape_modulation.parameter: transverse-to-axial modulus ratio, growth plate
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.conditions: E1/E3 = 4.55/0.47 for bovine growth plate; the same ratio in chondroepiphysis is 9.9
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.uncertainty: DERIVED BY THIS ATLAS from the two reported moduli; the paper does not state a ratio. THE LOADING MODES DIFFER AND THAT MUST NOT BE GLOSSED: E1 is a TENSILE modulus in the transverse plane and E3 a COMPRESSIVE modulus along the axis, so this is not one property measured in two directions. It is nevertheless the comparison the shape hypothesis needs, because those are precisely the modes a swelling cell imposes - expanding radially loads the surrounding matrix in circumferential TENSION, expanding axially loads the matrix above and below in COMPRESSION. A cell therefore meets roughly ten times more resistance going sideways than going up. Whether the ratio CHANGES with growth rate, age or load is unmeasured; cohen1998 and sergerie2009 each characterise a single state.

terminal_cell_shape_modulation.parameter: permeability, axial vs radial
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.conditions: bovine growth plate; axial k3 from confined compression, radial k1 from the unconfined fit
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.uncertainty: +/- 1.6 and +/- 1.8. Similar magnitude in both directions, so the anisotropy is in the solid matrix stiffness and not in fluid transport.

terminal_cell_shape_modulation.parameter: terminal hypertrophic cell height under hormone rescue
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.conditions: hypophysectomised rat proximal tibia after 8 d infusion - NaCl / IGF-I / GH / normal littermate. Proliferative phase 6.8 / 9.8 / 9.9 / 8.9; resting phase 3.9 / 3.9 / 4.7 / 5.9
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.uncertainty: NaCl significantly below the other three at proliferative and hypertrophic phases; the other three not significantly different from each other. Resting phase showed no significant difference between any group.

terminal_cell_shape_modulation.parameter: terminal hypertrophic cell volume under hormone rescue
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.conditions: same animals and groups as the height row - NaCl / IGF-I / GH / normal
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.uncertainty: NaCl significantly below the other three; the other three not different from each other. Net matrix production per cell did not differ by group OR by phase.

terminal_cell_shape_modulation.parameter: implied aspect ratio of the terminal cell under hormone rescue
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.conditions: NaCl / IGF-I / GH / normal, from the reported heights and volumes assuming a right circular cylinder
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.uncertainty: DERIVED BY THIS ATLAS under a geometric assumption the paper does not make - it reports height and volume and never diameter, so the diameter is back-calculated as 2*sqrt(V/pi*h). Read with that caveat, the pattern is that HORMONES RESTORE SIZE MORE COMPLETELY THAN SHAPE: IGF-I and GH bring volume to or above normal (9,890 and 11,140 against 10,246) while the aspect ratio reaches only 1.27 and 1.15 against a normal 1.42. This is consistent with the authors' own statement that cell productivity did not reach normal with either agent, and it suggests size and shape are separately regulated axes - which is the whole premise of this node. It is a derived quantity resting on one geometric assumption and should not be cited as a measurement.

terminal_cell_shape_modulation.parameter: axial vs transverse compliance of growth plate matrix
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.conditions: bovine growth plate and chondroepiphysis, unconfined compression fitted with a transversely isotropic biphasic model; axial = the longitudinal growth direction, transverse = radial. Permeability is of similar range in both directions but more variable axially, and the transverse Poisson's ratio is 2-3x the out-of-plane ratio
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.uncertainty: THE MECHANICAL ARCHITECTURE THE SHAPE HYPOTHESIS REQUIRES, AND IT WAS ALREADY MEASURED. A cell whose surrounding matrix resists lateral expansion roughly ten times more than axial expansion will convert a volume increase into HEIGHT rather than WIDTH with no active machinery at all. This atlas stated in docs/target_screen_round1.md rounds 5 and 6 that nobody had measured axial versus lateral anisotropy; that was wrong. Located via villemure2009 used as an index, which is what reviews are for. What remains genuinely unmeasured is whether the ratio CHANGES with growth rate - a static anisotropy explains how a cell could be shaped, not why the shaping varies.

terminal_cell_shape_modulation.parameter: volume versus height as predictors of longitudinal bone growth
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.conditions: mouse proximal tibia, distal tibia and distal ulna compared against each other; hundreds of thousands of chondrocytes by PACT-deCAL clearing, light-sheet imaging and 3D segmentation (3D MAPs)
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.uncertainty: DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS the premise of this node, in the best-powered measurement available. The authors state that hypertrophic cell volume is a better predictor of longitudinal bone growth than hypertrophic cell height, with cell diameter correlated to only some of the differences. THE COMPARISON IS BETWEEN GROWTH PLATES, however - proximal tibia versus distal tibia versus distal ulna - which is the same spatial axis on which breur1991 found r=0.98 for volume. hunziker1989 compared one plate at two AGES and found volume falling 13% while growth rose 20%. So the two need not conflict: volume may predict between plates while height carries change within a plate over time. Nobody has applied a modern 3D method to the within-plate temporal comparison, and until someone does, this node rests on a single unreplicated n=6 study from 1989 against a 10^5-cell 3D dataset pointing the other way.

terminal_cell_shape_modulation.parameter: fraction of total chondrocyte volume increase occurring BEFORE the hypertrophic zone
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.conditions: mouse growth plates; volume rises 20% resting to proliferative, 74% proliferative to prehypertrophic, 50% prehypertrophic to hypertrophic, about ninefold overall. Surface area rises fivefold with 70% of the increase before the hypertrophic zone
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.uncertainty: contradicts the standing paradigm that most enlargement happens in the hypertrophic zone, which is an assumption embedded in the atlas flow model's h_term term and in every therapeutic programme aimed at hypertrophic enlargement. If most of the volume is acquired prehypertrophically, the terminal cell height is a readout of an earlier process rather than the process itself.

terminal_cell_shape_modulation.parameter: aspect ratio, resting versus hypertrophic chondrocytes
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.conditions: mouse; cells go round (resting) to flat and elongated (proliferative) to round and large (hypertrophic), so shape changes only across the first three zones and returns
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.uncertainty: the authors note this means chondrocytes could in theory have grown isometrically throughout, and suggest the allometric route is chosen TO PREVENT EXPANSION OF THE BONE CIRCUMFERENCE DURING ELONGATION - which is the anisotropic-constraint argument stated from the cell's side rather than the matrix's. Measured across the differentiation axis, not across growth rates.

terminal_cell_shape_modulation.parameter: transverse-to-axial modulus ratio across developmental stage
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.conditions: porcine distal ulnar growth plate at newborn (n=24), 4 weeks group A (n=11), 4 weeks group B (n=15), 8 weeks (n=28) and 18 weeks (n=14); E1/E3 from a transversely isotropic biphasic fit using the cohen1998 model
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.uncertainty: DERIVED BY THIS ATLAS as E1/E3 from the paper's Table 2; the paper reports the moduli separately and never the ratio. THE ANISOTROPY COLLAPSES ROUGHLY TEN-FOLD ACROSS DEVELOPMENT, from strongly transversely stiff at birth to essentially isotropic by 8-18 weeks, over exactly the period in which porcine growth rate falls. The newborn value of 11.0 independently reproduces cohen1998's 9.7 in newborn bovine. THIS IS A CORRELATION ACROSS AGES, NOT AN INTERVENTION - plate thickness falls 3508 to 1800 um over the same period and many things fall with age. The 4-week animals split into two subgroups whose E1 differs 24-fold (9.74 vs 0.41 MPa) at the same nominal age, which the authors attribute to rapid developmental change at 3-4 weeks and which means developmental stage is not cleanly defined there.

terminal_cell_shape_modulation.parameter: out-of-plane and transverse moduli by developmental stage
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.conditions: porcine distal ulna at newborn, 4W(a), 4W(b), 8W, 18W; mean with 95% CI in the source
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.uncertainty: 95% CIs 0.05-0.14 on E3 and 0.06-2.11 on E1. A second fitting method gives somewhat different E1 (6.71 newborn, 0.52 at 18W) but the same direction and the same collapse.

terminal_cell_shape_modulation.parameter: human terminal hypertrophic cell HEIGHT and WIDTH in the same cells
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.conditions: human vertebral body physis; 13 severe-scoliosis patients sampled at the convex-side apex (mean curve 67 +/- 23 degrees) against 5 age-matched autopsy controls without scoliosis. Hypertrophic zone height 152 +/- 34 vs 180 +/- 42 um (p=0.21, ns)
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.uncertainty: THE FIRST HUMAN MEASUREMENT OF CELL HEIGHT AND WIDTH IN THE SAME CELLS. Height differs by 34% (p<0.0005) while WIDTH IS ESSENTIALLY IDENTICAL (14.9 +/- 1.5 vs 15.0 +/- 2.5, ns). Implied aspect ratios 0.57 and 0.85, a 33% difference. Caveats that matter: this is VERTEBRAL not long-bone physis; the scoliosis group is heterogeneous by aetiology (idiopathic, congenital, neurofibromatosis, neuromuscular, Marfan); controls are n=5 autopsy specimens; and no growth rate was measured in either group, so this shows height varying where width does not, NOT height tracking growth.

terminal_cell_shape_modulation.parameter: human terminal cell height and diameter
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.conditions: human growth plate, any site, any age
terminal_cell_shape_modulation.uncertainty: PARTLY SUPERSEDED 2026-08-06 by bylskiaustrow2018, which measures both in human VERTEBRAL physis. For LONG BONE the absence stands. RECORDED AS AN ABSENCE. thurston1985 and kember1976 both report a human hypertrophic cell HEIGHT (and disagree, 20.5 vs 33 um, contradiction C-L1-07). Neither reports the transverse diameter in the same cells, so no human aspect ratio exists and the one quantity hunziker1989 identifies as the carrier of growth-rate change has never been measured in a human.

reliability_policy: Phase 2e. Disputes in this atlas are NOT encoded as duplicate rows - ~94% of parameter names appear once. They are encoded in the row's own uncertainty/conditions text or in a range-valued `value`. single_source_point_no_uncertainty is the RISK class: one source, a point value, and no stated uncertainty.

superseded_rows.parameter: duration of food restriction inducing growth-plate LEPROT/LEPROTL1
superseded_rows.conditions: was 4 weeks, wild-type versus Fgf21-knockout mouse tibial growth plate (wu2013)
superseded_rows.uncertainty: ROW VOIDED BY CORR-004. The source, wu2013, was withdrawn by J Biol Chem in 2020 (notice PMID 32917830). Retained as a tombstone so that anyone who saw the number in an earlier version of this atlas can find out what happened to it. Do not use the value. source_ref points at wu2012 only because the schema requires a resolvable reference; wu2012 does not contain this measurement.
superseded_rows.superseded_model: wu2013 in vivo LEPROT/LEPROTL1 induction - withdrawn, not superseded

superseded_rows.parameter: Fraction of mouse bone PPi attributable to Ank activity (older estimate)
superseded_rows.conditions: prior literature estimate, now reinterpreted as ANK-driven ATP feeding ENPP1
superseded_rows.uncertainty: cited by the authors as the figure their data reinterpret

superseded_rows.parameter: Effect of homozygous Col10a1 deletion on long bone length in mouse
superseded_rows.note: The measurement stands - no detectable long-bone length difference was reported. What is superseded is its use as evidence that the null has no phenotype. Gress 2000 re-examined the SAME null line and found ~14% growth plate width reduction, proliferative-zone-dominant compression and ~14% lethality. See CORR-002.

unverified_rows.parameter: ratio of exposure duration, navepegritide-released CNP to vosoritide
